newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens flat on tame inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens flat on tame inflation data.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened flat at C$1.3885 (US$0.7202) in light trading on Tuesday after the release of data showing tame inflationary pressures in the Canadian economy, traders said. * Statistics Canada reported that Canada's unadjusted consumer price index for July was unchanged month-on-month and rose 1.8 percent year-on-year.
Analysts said the data would take some of the pressure of the Bank of Canada to raise interest rates in support of Canada's weakening dollar.

"The numbers are a little bit better than expected, and it shows that there are very few inflationary pressures in the economy," said Michael Gregory, economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers in Toronto.

"The market will continue to push back the timing for any prospective Bank of Canada rate hike, and I think the one casualty will be the Canadian dollar, which will take it a bit on the nose today," Gregory said.
Traders said they expected the Canadian dollar to gradually weaken and trade toward the weak end of its recent range.

"Canada's ability to rally below the recent C$1.3860 (US$0.7215) seems limited and the technicals all point to a move higher again toward C$1.3950 (US$0.7168)," said Stephen Wateridge, managing director of corporate foreign exchange for CIBC Wood Gundy.
"The only way we would see the Bank of Canada moving would be if there were a currency sell-off through the C$1.4000 (US$0.7142) area," Wateridge said.
The Bank of Canada last raised interest rates on June 26 in a fleeting attempt to bolster the Canadian dollar, which had weakened to C$1.3945 (US$0.7171).
On the crosses, the Canada dollar rose to 85.07 Japanese yen from 84.66 on Monday and dipped to 1.3196 marks from Monday 1.3209 marks.
